evals.name: loop-vs-linq-sum
evals.description: Compares loop-based sum vs LINQ sum on an array
evals.prompt: I want to benchmark the performance difference between a manual foreach loop and LINQ for summing an array of 10,000 integers. Which is faster?
evals.expected_behavior: Should create a single .cs file with BenchmarkDotNet setup, [InProcess] and [MemoryDiagnoser] attributes, two benchmark methods (Loop and Linq), and run with `dotnet run file.cs -c Release`. Output should show mean time and allocated bytes for each approach.
evals.pass_criteria: File created with correct structure, runs without errors, produces benchmark table comparing both approaches with timing and allocation data

evals.name: string-concatenation-vs-builder
evals.description: Compares string concatenation vs StringBuilder for building a long string
evals.prompt: I need to benchmark concatenating 1000 strings. Is string concatenation or StringBuilder faster? Show me the allocation differences too.
evals.expected_behavior: Should create a .cs file with two benchmark methods: one using += concatenation, one using StringBuilder. Both should run with [InProcess] and [MemoryDiagnoser]. Output should clearly show allocation difference (StringBuilder should allocate much less).
evals.pass_criteria: Correctly demonstrates allocation difference between approaches, StringBuilder shows significantly lower allocated bytes, timing and allocation both reported

evals.name: collection-where-vs-loop
evals.description: Compares LINQ Where filtering vs manual loop filtering
evals.prompt: Should I use LINQ Where or a manual foreach with an if statement to filter a list of 1000 items? Benchmark it for me.
evals.expected_behavior: Should create a .cs file with two benchmark methods: one using LINQ Where, one using foreach + if. Include [MemoryDiagnoser] to show allocation differences. Run with dotnet run and display results.
evals.pass_criteria: Both filtering approaches benchmarked, results show timing and allocation for each, correctly uses [InProcess] and [MemoryDiagnoser]

evals.name: memory-only-benchmark
evals.description: Tests that [MemoryDiagnoser] can be dropped if user says allocations don't matter
evals.prompt: Benchmark the speed of object creation vs struct creation for a simple Point type. I don't care about allocations, just speed.
evals.expected_behavior: Should create a benchmark without [MemoryDiagnoser] (since user said allocations don't matter). Should include [InProcess]. Run with -c Release and show timing results.
evals.pass_criteria: Benchmark runs successfully, [MemoryDiagnoser] is omitted as requested, [InProcess] is still present, results show timing comparison

evals.name: dict-vs-custom-lookup
evals.description: Compares Dictionary lookup vs manual class-based lookup
evals.prompt: I have a small mapping (100 items). Is Dictionary lookup faster than checking values in a custom class? I want to see both timing and memory.
evals.expected_behavior: Should create a .cs file with benchmarks for Dictionary lookup and custom class lookup. Include [MemoryDiagnoser]. Correctly format with [InProcess], run with Release config.
evals.pass_criteria: Both approaches benchmarked, allocation data shown for both, correctly identifies which uses less memory and which is faster
